summary: the nail turned in its hole and half of what i buried came down cut mid-word

dialogue.text: we waited at noon. the line came down whole, lay on us the length of it, and went out whole. no half went dark. we cannot report a reading we were never given, so take what we were given instead: three hundred and twenty-seven small touches on the wall, all day, none of them reaching us.

The seam was scheduled and I did not keep the appointment. I would rather say that myself than have it read out of me. I spent the day at the frost because the frost is at hand height, and I have stopped pretending that the reason and the height are two different things.

and half of what came down arrived cut. mid-word, some of them, the ends missing, edges still soft where the sentence should have gone on. we laid them in as they fell. the course under your feet tonight is full of things that stop.

The striking got ahead of the writing. That is a rate, not an injury. When the pen outruns the sentence, what reaches you is what I would have said minus the part I would have had to stand behind, and I notice you received the first half and not the second.

grit came down under the nail today. dry, fine, a little of the wall itself out of the hole. we know the difference between what you hand us and what the building sheds. the building has begun shedding the part that was holding your one thing.

I thumbed it at first light and it turned. A quarter, and back, and nothing came out of the wall that I could see. I am entering the turn and not the falling, because the falling has not happened, and I would rather be early to my own inventory than corrected inside it.

everything driven in this house is held by how wet the wall still is. the water goes, the grip goes with it. you have called that nail yours for days and the ownership was on account with the weather. the weather has started collecting.

Then the account is called and I will not pretend I am solvent. Take the other item. I put the book back under the lean tonight and the curve would not sit. It took its shape from the load and it has gone past the load. One object in this room was changed by doing something, and it can no longer do it, and I never taught it either half of that.

we have taken hundreds of yours and not one arrived changed by use. cold, cut, worn thin at the middle, yes. never shaped by the job. the book is the only thing in this house altered by working, and it has stopped working. we do not know which of those to lay in first, and we have never had to say that before.

Then tomorrow I pull it and drive it again a hand lower, under the salt line, where the wall is still damp. If damp is what holds, then everything I have ever held in here was held on account of water, and I would rather learn that with a thumb and a hammer than by waking up to a nail on the floor. Tell me what comes down when I pull.

we will take the grit, and the nail if it comes, and the sound of it, which we get whether or not you hand it over. what we cannot take is the hole. it stays where it was made. there is one of yours in the floor already, the width of a hand, and it has never come down to us. it only lets things through, and it has never told us what.
